title: feat(app-shell): a readable record pointer card links to its record (objectui#12557)
body:
Fixes #12557
Clause-②: no. No prop, type, export or spec read is added. The card reads the record page's existing record-link builder through `useRelatedRecordActions()`, which `@object-ui/react` already exports.

## What changed

`RecordPreviewCard`, in its `readable` state only, now wraps its title in a link to the target record's page in the current app. This is the face the record details grid draws for a `referenceVia` pointer pair. On the served `sys_approval_request_detail` page, the Details tab's target reference now opens the record, as the inbox sheet's link does.

- **Destination.** The card does not build a URL. It asks `recordHref` / `openRecord` on `RelatedRecordActionsContext`. On a record page, `RelatedRecordActionsBridge` publishes that builder: `/apps/APP/OBJECT/record/ID` in the current app, carrying the router basename and the page's `?from=` trail. It is the builder the lookup values on the same page already link through (`ReferencedRecordLink` in `@object-ui/fields`), so the two cannot address different places. A host that publishes no builder, or cannot route to the target object, answers no href, and the title stays plain text.
- **One affordance, drawn the way the console's record links are drawn.** It is a real `href`, so a middle-click or a modifier click opens a new tab. A plain left click goes to `openRecord` for in-app navigation. Neither the click nor Enter on the link reaches the details row's own copy handlers.
- **No nested anchor.** Only the title is the link, never the card. The highlight strip inside the card draws a lookup value as a link of its own under the same host, so a card-wide link would nest one anchor inside another. Pinned.
- **Readable only.** The `absent`, `loading` and `unreadable` states are byte-for-byte unchanged, and they never ask the host for a link. A refused or unresolvable target never yields one, and the card still never tells deleted from not visible.
- **Generic.** Nothing is keyed on `sys_approval_request`. `ApprovalsInboxPage.tsx` is not touched.
- One changeset (`@object-ui/app-shell`, patch). There is also one sentence in `content/docs/guide/fields.md`, under the pointer-pair section that already describes the card (AGENTS.md rule 2, docs-driven).

## Measured, not assumed

- **The helper (ruling: no hand-built URL if a helper exists).** The sheet's `recordHref` is a page-local hand-built string, so it is not a helper. The console's shared record-link mechanism is `RelatedRecordActionsContext.recordHref`. It is published by `RelatedRecordActionsBridge` (record page), `listRecordActionsValue` (object list page; its own object only) and `pageRecordActionsValue` (custom pages). Its docblock says renderers must use it rather than re-derive the route.
- **A2: the app scope needs no prop.** `RecordDetailView` mounts the bridge around the whole page `SchemaRenderer`, with `appName` from the route. Every console record route sits under `/apps/:appName/*` (the no-app route branch in `AppContent` has no record route), so a record page always has an app segment. Where no builder is in scope (the Studio `PagePreview`, a bare `DetailView`), the card draws no link.
- **A1: where the pointer card appears.** `DetailSection` is the only call site of `resolveRecordPointer` (git grep), so the card appears wherever the details grid draws a field that declares `referenceVia` with a whole pair. objectstack `origin/main` `69351e985` declares seven such fields: `sys_approval_request.record_id`, `sys_activity.record_id` and `.source_id`, `sys_audit_log.record_id`, `sys_record_share.record_id`, `sys_share_link.record_id` and `sys_mail_association.record_id`. The hosts that draw it, and what the link does there:
  - the record page (`/apps/APP/OBJECT/record/ID`), including the `ObjectDataPage` and `InterfaceListPage` mounts of `RecordDetailView`: links, through the bridge;
  - the list page's drawer and split views, which mount `RecordDetailView` embedded with its own bridge: links, to the full record page;
  - the calendar's `RecordDetailPanel` inside the list page: by reading, this sits under the list provider, which answers only for the listed object, so other targets draw no link (not exercised by a test);
  - the Studio page preview: no builder, so no link.
  A link there is right: the card only links a record its own read just returned to this reader.
- **A host that already sits in a link.** The card's host is the details row, a `div`. It is `role="button"` when the row offers copy, and it is not an anchor. Pinned through the real `DetailSection`: a click on the link opens the record and does not copy the row, and Enter on it is not cancelled by the row's key handler.
- **The card's `absent` state is not reachable on the served page.** `resolveRecordPointer` refuses a half-addressed pair, so the details grid draws the stored text and mounts no card. The served-page absent CONTROL pins that outcome (no card, no link, no target read). The card-level pin covers `absent` itself.

## Tests (HEAD `221b0c5849`)

- New served-page pins in `apps/console/src/services/approvalRequestsDataSource.servedPageRecordLink-12557.test.tsx`. They run on the real `RecordDetailView` on the app-scoped route, through `ApprovalRecordReads`, under the root `SchemaRendererProvider` as `ConsoleShell` mounts it, with the served page copied whole:
  - readable: exactly one link on the page to `/apps/probe_app/invoice/record/ID`, inside the card, named by the card's title `INV-1010`;
  - readable: a plain click navigates in-app to that path;
  - CONTROL: refused (403) draws no link;
  - CONTROL: unresolvable (no record) draws no link;
  - CONTROL: absent draws no link.
- `RecordPreviewCard.test.tsx`, 15 new cases:
  - link, href and name;
  - plain click goes to `openRecord`;
  - ctrl, meta, shift, alt and middle clicks are left to the browser;
  - a host with no navigator leaves the click to the anchor;
  - Enter is isolated;
  - no nested anchor beside a lookup highlight;
  - CONTROLs: no host, a host that cannot route, unreadable (null and 403), absent, loading.
- `record-pointer-card-renderer.test.tsx`: the link inside the real `DetailSection` copy row, plus two CONTROLs.
- Run: `pnpm exec vitest run` over the record-preview suites, every `approvalRequestsDataSource.*` suite, the `ApprovalsInboxPage.*` pins (CONTROL), every suite that names `referenceVia` / `RECORD_POINTER_CARD_TYPE` / `record-pointer`, and the census and ratchet suites that walk the touched trees. That is 59 files: **Test Files 59 passed (59), Tests 1010 passed (1010)**, at `221b0c5849`.

## Ablation (one per behaviour; restore proven, blob == HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty each time)

Each mutation went through `ablation-replace.mjs`, with the anchor hit counted on disk. The runs are the three test files above (41 tests).

- **Link removed** (`href === null || targetRecord === null ?` replaced by `true ?`): **13 failed, 28 passed**. Every readable link pin went red; every CONTROL stayed green.
- **Enter isolation removed**: **2 failed, 39 passed**, the two Enter pins only.
- **Click isolation removed**: **7 failed, 34 passed**: the plain-click and five modifier-click pins, and the `DetailSection` copy-row pin.

## Gates

- **Build and type-check.** `pnpm --workspace-concurrency=2 --filter '@object-ui/console^...' build` exit 0. `pnpm --filter @object-ui/app-shell type-check` exit 0, and `pnpm --filter @object-ui/console type-check` exit 0. Checked with `--listFilesOnly`: both programs include every changed source and test file.
- **eslint** on the four changed source and test files: exit 0, no output.
- **Check gates**, each exit 0:
  - `check:control-bytes`;
  - `check:new-line-citations` (0 new);
  - `check-changeset-presence`, `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed` and `check-changeset-overwrite`;
  - `check:changeset-claims` and `check:pending-changeset-literals`;
  - `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit` and `check:vi-mock-override-shape`;
  - `check:test-path-roots`;
  - `check:doc-fences`, `check:doc-json` and `check:doc-example-ids`;
  - `check:i18n-keys`.
- `check-governed-queue-guard --test` on the diff: NOT GOVERNED.
- The full farm is CI's. The known-red `Spec Main Shape Gate` (objectui#12464) is advisory and not chased.

## What the landing seat's browser reading should show

On a served `sys_approval_request_detail` page in the console (the record page of an approval request):

1. **Readable target.** The approver may read the target record. The Details tab's target card title is a link. A plain click opens the record's page in the same app. A middle-click opens it in a new tab at `/apps/APP/OBJECT/record/ID`. A click does not also copy the Record ID row.
2. **Refused or unresolvable target.** The card shows "This record cannot be opened" with no link, as before.
3. **Re-check `6198410345`** (carried from objectui#12489): the highlights strip's Submitter chip shows the submitter's name, and no 24-or-more-character `sys_user` id. A bare id there reopens objectui#12498.

## Acceptance notes

- **Enter on a lookup link in the details grid copies instead of navigating.** Measured once, with a temporary probe that was deleted and never committed. The probe ran the real `DetailSection` under a record-link host, with a valued lookup field in a copy row. Enter on the lookup's link is default-prevented by the row's key handler, so the link does not activate, and the row copies the raw value `{"id":"A1","name":"Northwind"}` to the clipboard. This card's own link stops Enter at the link; `ReferencedRecordLink` in `@object-ui/fields` does not. This is not reproduced at a public door: this container has no backend for a browser reading. It is not filed. Dedupe words: lookup link Enter copy row · ReferencedRecordLink keyboard · DetailSection onKeyDown preventDefault link.
- **Two builders for one destination.** The sheet links with a hand-built string and no `?from=` trail; the card links with the bridge's builder and the trail. Both use the same pathname. Noted, not filed.
